skill.name: signal-slack-alerts
skill.description: Watches a list of target accounts for new hiring and leadership signals and posts a short, deduplicated alert for each one to a Slack channel. Reads careers pages with scrape_jobs and re-checks tracked leaders with enrich_person. Use when someone asks to get Slack alerts for hiring signals, watch target accounts, or flag new leaders and job changes at named accounts.
skill.summary: Track hiring and leadership changes at selected companies and post deduplicated alerts to Slack.
skill.author: leadsets

security_audit.summary: The Leadsets endpoint supports the intended workflow but receives company and tracked contact inputs. The other static flags reflect formatting or routine documentation, with no evidence of shell execution, environment reads, host reconnaissance, or embedded prompt injection. Slack alerts can disclose contact emails without a separate approval check, and an interrupted run can repeat posts before the snapshot is saved.

remediation.issue: Contact emails can be shared in Slack without a channel access check.
remediation.suggestion: Omit emails by default. Require explicit approval for email sharing and verify the destination and its audience before posting.

remediation.issue: The workflow sends company and contact inputs to Leadsets.
remediation.suggestion: Disclose what Leadsets receives before the first run. Send only the public careers URLs and contact identifiers needed for the requested checks.

remediation.issue: Slack posts can succeed before their alert IDs are recorded.
remediation.suggestion: Record each confirmed post immediately. Reconcile pending alert IDs against Slack before retrying after an interruption.

semantic_findings.title: Slack Alerts Can Disclose Contact Emails
semantic_findings.description: The output includes verified and labeled catch-all addresses in the selected Slack channel. The workflow does not require approval to share those addresses or check who can read them.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The output explicitly includes contact email addresses. Email verification does not authorize disclosure to channel members.

semantic_findings.title: Interrupted Runs Can Repeat Slack Posts
semantic_findings.description: The workflow posts alerts before saving their IDs. If posting succeeds but the snapshot is not saved, a rerun can post the same alerts again.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: Deduplication relies on IDs from the previous snapshot. The posting step specifies no recovery check for messages already sent during an interrupted run.

content.user_title: Send Hiring and Leadership Alerts to Slack
content.value_statement: Checking company careers pages and leadership changes by hand takes time. This skill checks your watchlist and posts new findings to Slack without repeating alerts recorded in the last snapshot.
actual_capabilities: Checks remaining Leadsets scrape units and enrichment records before processing the watchlist.
Reads public careers pages and filters openings by watched role keywords and search dates.
Compares tracked leaders with the saved snapshot to find changes in title or company.
Groups signals into one Slack message per account and skips alert IDs recorded in the previous snapshot.
Saves roles, leader details, and posted alert IDs for the next run.
Returns a run summary with remaining quotas, missing results, and deferred accounts.
limitations: Hiring checks require Leadsets scrape units on a paid plan and only cover public careers pages.
Leadership checks are limited to the contacts you provide and use Leadsets enrichment records.
Posting requires the agent to have access to the chosen Slack channel.
Repeat detection depends on a saved snapshot. An interrupted run may repeat posts that were not recorded.

use_cases.title: Watch a short list of companies
use_cases.description: Check target companies for new sales openings and send the results to a private team channel.

use_cases.title: Review changes among tracked executives
use_cases.description: Track known contacts for moves into watched senior roles or changes of company before planning outreach.

use_cases.title: Run a weekly account check
use_cases.description: Use the latest saved snapshot to report new signals and identify accounts deferred because of usage limits.

prompt_templates.title: Check one company
prompt_templates.prompt: Check [careers page] for RevOps openings posted in the last 14 days. Show me the results without posting to Slack.

prompt_templates.title: Post hiring alerts from a watchlist
prompt_templates.prompt: Read [watchlist] and check for new SDR and BDR roles. Post one alert per matching company to [approved Slack channel] without contact emails.

prompt_templates.title: Compare tracked leaders with a snapshot
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [tracked leaders] with [previous snapshot]. Report moves to a new company or into a VP or executive role. Preview alerts without posting or sharing emails.

prompt_templates.title: Run a quota-aware weekly check
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [watchlist], [tracked leaders], and [previous snapshot] to check for changes since the last run. Check Leadsets quotas and prioritize [priority accounts]. Post only new alerts to [approved Slack channel], omit contact emails, and report deferred accounts.

output_examples.input: Check a watchlist for new RevOps openings and post results without contact emails.
output: Example Company: Hiring. Revenue Operations Analyst, posted May 12. Source: company careers page.
Checked three companies and posted one alert. Skipped one signal already recorded in the snapshot.

output_examples.input: Compare tracked leaders with the last snapshot and summarize the run.
output_examples.output: Checked five tracked leaders and found one company change. One contact was not found. Posted one leadership alert and saved the updated snapshot.

best_practices: Start with one careers page to check role names and dates before processing the rest of the watchlist.
Confirm who can read the Slack channel and omit contact emails unless sharing is approved.
Keep the latest snapshot. After an interruption, compare it with Slack before posting again.
anti_patterns: Running a large first batch without checking quotas and testing the role filters.
Treating a verified or catch-all email as permission to share it in Slack.
Deleting the previous snapshot and expecting the same alerts to be skipped.

faq.question: What accounts and connections do I need?
faq.answer: Use a Leadsets account with MCP or the Leadsets REST API. For posting, the agent also needs a Slack connection with access to the chosen channel.

faq.question: Can I check hiring signals on the free Leadsets plan?
faq.answer: No. Job scraping requires scrape units on a paid plan. You can request leadership checks instead when enrichment records are available.

faq.question: Do I need to provide a list of leaders?
faq.answer: No. Without a tracked contact list, the skill checks hiring signals only. It does not discover new leaders.

faq.question: How far back does the skill check?
faq.answer: The default is 14 days, or since the last run if a snapshot exists. You can specify a different lookback period.

faq.question: How does the skill avoid posting the same signal again?
faq.answer: It compares signals with alert IDs in the previous snapshot. After an interrupted run, check the Slack channel for posts that were not recorded.

faq.question: Does the skill contact prospects?
faq.answer: No. It posts alerts to the selected Slack channel and does not send outreach. Ask it to omit contact emails from the alerts.
